exposure: Maternal disease (gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, perinatal infection)
Food habits (normal diet, sugar diet, fatty diet)
cohort: The study included 170 children and adolescents diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus at a special center in Sulaimani city, with data on risk factors collected from their mothers or fathers.
finding: Age at diagnosis and mode of delivery were identified as the most significant factors affecting Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus, with early childhood years also playing a vital role.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was considered the first most significant factor affecting Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
cross-section timing: Data was collected cross-sectionally from parents of children and adolescents previously diagnosed with Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus.
birth_weight: Neonatal weight was assessed as a potential factor.
gest_age: Gestational age at birth was assessed as a potential factor.
